scope: Temples, shrines, pagodas and monasteries of East and South-East Asia
Temples and sacred sites of ancient Greece, Rome, Egypt, Mesopotamia and Persia
Sacred and ceremonial sites of the Americas, Africa and Oceania (not the step pyramid: already made)
Churches, chapels, abbeys, mosques, synagogues and cloisters of Europe, North Africa and the Middle East
Towers that are not lighthouses, castles or wizard towers: watchtowers, bell towers, water towers, signal towers, minarets, fire lookouts
Forts, gatehouses, palisades, town walls, bunkers, border posts and siege works (no castles)
Ruins and digs: ruined towns, excavations, standing stones, tombs, burial mounds, abandoned quarries
Fantasy buildings: elven halls, dwarven gates, goblin shacks, dragon roosts, giant's houses, floating keeps (not the wizard's tower: already made)
Fantasy places that are not buildings first: enchanted groves, fairy rings, portals, crystal caverns, witch's gardens, troll bridges
Science-fiction exteriors: moon and Mars bases, landing pads, asteroid mines, orbital docks, alien monoliths
Science-fiction interiors shown as cutaways: ship bridges, reactor rooms, cryo bays, hydroponics, airlocks (not a plain corridor: already made)
Near-future and cyberpunk city fragments: neon alleys, capsule hotels, rooftop antenna farms, drone ports, vending corners
Rural dwellings around the world: cabins, huts, yurts, igloos, stilt houses, treehouses, roundhouses (not a plain house, not a farm)
Town buildings seen from outside with a little of their surroundings: bakery, inn, bookshop, post office, fire station, town hall, cinema
Markets, stalls and street food: night market, flower stall, noodle cart, fishmonger, bazaar lane, flea market
Workshops and crafts, as yards or cutaways: blacksmith, potter, glassblower, cooper, weaver, shipwright, luthier
Industry and energy: mines, derricks, dams, sawmills, kilns, foundries, power stations, wind and solar plants
Mills and waterworks: watermills, windmills, wells, aqueducts, canal locks, pump houses, irrigation wheels
Bridges and crossings: rope, stone arch, covered, draw, suspension and pontoon bridges, fords, ferry landings, stepping stones
Railways and tramways: halts, signal boxes, engine sheds, turntables, funiculars, cable cars, mine railways, level crossings
Roads and roadsides: fuel stations, bus shelters, toll booths, diners, motels, rest areas, road works, drive-ins (no street corner)
Boats and shores: fishing piers, boathouses, slipways, dry docks, shipwrecks on a beach, canal moorings, ferry slips (no harbour, no lighthouse)
Under the sea: reefs, sunken ships, diving bells, underwater labs, kelp forests, hydrothermal vents, lost statues
Flight: hangars, airship masts, balloon launches, helipads, control towers, bush airstrips, glider winches (no rocket)
Mountains and caves: alpine huts, summit shelters, cave mouths, cliff dwellings, via ferrata, mountain passes, glacier camps
Forest and jungle places: ranger stations, canopy walkways, logging camps, hidden waterfalls, hides, charcoal burners (no plain campsite)
Deserts and canyons: caravanserais, mesa pueblos, desert wells, rock arches, salt works, sandstone tombs, nomad tents (not the desert island: already made)
Polar and winter places: ice-fishing huts, research stations, ski lifts, frozen falls, snow forts, husky kennels (no snowman as the subject)
Tropical islands and beaches: tiki huts, lagoons, lifeguard towers, tide pools, beach bars, surf shacks, turtle beaches
Rivers, lakes and wetlands: stilt fishing shacks, beaver dams, lily ponds with pavilions, swamp boardwalks, weirs, houseboats
Gardens and garden buildings: zen gardens, hedge mazes, greenhouses, gazebos, topiary, walled gardens, orangeries (no park, no playground)
Growing places that are not a farmyard: vineyards, rice terraces, tea slopes, orchards, apiaries, hop gardens, lavender fields (no barn, silo or tractor scene)
Monuments and memorials: obelisks, triumphal arches, colossal statues, fountain plazas, sundials, war memorials, totem poles
Sport and games places: skate ramps, mini-golf holes, ski jumps, boxing rings, archery ranges, bowling greens, climbing walls (no playground)
Fairs, festivals and stages: carousels, big wheels, bandstands, puppet theatres, lantern festivals, maypoles, circus rings
Expeditions and working camps: dig camps, base camps, safari camps, pirate hideouts, gold-rush claims, surveyors' camps (not a plain campsite)
Rooms shown as cutaways: library nook, bathhouse, wine cellar, attic, throne room, observatory dome, greenhouse lab (no living room, kitchen, bedroom or desk)
Shop interiors shown as cutaways: clock repairer, apothecary, tailor, record shop, toy shop, cheese shop, bicycle shop
Everyday places of the ancient and early medieval world: cave camps, roundhouses, Roman baths, longhouses, granaries, forums, villas
Scenes from myth and legend: a sword in a stone, a wooden horse at a gate, a labyrinth entrance, a world tree, an ark on a mountain
Miniature and toy worlds: dolls' house rooms, board-game islands, snow-globe villages, terrariums, toy forts, model villages
A vehicle at rest in its place: a steam engine at a water tower, a covered wagon at a ford, a submarine in its pen, a tram at its stop (no car as the subject)
Places made by or for animals: beehives, seabird cliffs, anthills in cutaway, dinosaur nests, stable yards, dovecotes, sheepfolds
Abandoned and overgrown places: a rusting fairground ride, a bus in the woods, a ghost-town saloon, a flooded chapel, a derelict greenhouse
